# Appeal of Denial — Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**Governing Policy:** Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404, Shoulder Arthroscopy — https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf

**Member:** Cameron Grant
**Member ID:** W314904804
**Plan:** Molina Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), Arizona
**Denial date:** 2026-08-08
**Reference number:** POC-9DD444765E-23652
**Procedure:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827

Dear Molina Healthcare,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-08, reference number POC-9DD444765E-23652. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Molina to reconsider its decision.

## Why I believe this decision should be reconsidered

Molina's own Shoulder Arthroscopy policy (MCP-404) sets out the criteria the plan uses to decide whether shoulder arthroscopy procedures are medically necessary. The section on diagnostic arthroscopy states:

> "Diagnostic arthroscopy may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> " Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My records establish both of these elements:

- **Severe, disabling pain and loss of function:** I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side. These are basic, age-appropriate daily activities that this injury has taken from me.
- **Failure of non-surgical management for at least three months, including at least two approaches:** I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (20 visits, 2026-05-20 through 2026-07-15) focused on rotator cuff strengthening, documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief, and I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-08 that gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief. That is three separate non-surgical treatments, well beyond the two the policy requires, over a period far longer than three months.

The policy also references, in connection with these criteria:

> "and  Demonstration of functionally limited range of motion (active or passive) on physical examination as compared to the non-involved side  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration, including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My exam findings document positive provocative testing and range of motion limited by pain on the affected side. My records as provided to me do not include a side-to-side comparison of range of motion, so I am not in a position to state that this specific element has been documented one way or the other — I am simply noting what the exam findings say and ask that this be considered alongside the rest of my clinical picture.

I also want to note, in fairness to the review process, that the citations I have been given from MCP-404 include headings for arthroscopic debridement, loose body removal, synovectomy, labral repair/biceps tenodesis, distal clavicle excision/subacromial decompression, capsulorrhaphy, and capsular release for frozen shoulder — but none of these excerpts is specifically labeled for rotator cuff repair, and several of the headings I have are not followed by the actual listed criteria. I am not able to quote a rotator-cuff-repair-specific standard because one was not provided to me, and I do not want to guess at what the plan's specific criteria are. This is part of why I am requesting, below, that Molina identify exactly which criteria were applied to my case.

My MRI from 2026-06-05 confirms a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke — nothing in my record suggests a reason surgery would be unsafe or inappropriate.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

Because Molina's utilization management materials state that the criteria used for review are MCG guidelines available to providers through the secure portal, and that members may call to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination, I am requesting that Molina provide me, in writing, the MCG guideline title and criteria applied to my determination. I would like to compare that specific guideline, criterion by criterion, against my medical records.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Molina to reverse this denial and approve coverage for my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), or, at minimum, to identify the specific criteria applied to my case so that my surgeon and I can address any remaining questions directly.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-04, as stated in my denial notice, and I understand that the appeal address printed on that notice is the correct one to use. I will also submit this appeal through the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com and am available by phone at the number on my member ID card if any additional information is needed.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Cameron Grant
Member ID: W314904804
Date: [DATE]
Contact phone: [PHONE NUMBER]
Contact address: [ADDRESS]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
